source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

method: Pinned Greek read completely before authoring; all 108 verses drafted before reading prior Fluent. TSW compared programmatically after authoring, not used as a base. Every verse carries a source-specific decision. No word-change quota.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned opening without adding Son of God from the variant.
verses.before: The beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ.
verses.after: The beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: The beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.

verses.rationale: Preserves Isaiah attribution and the messenger’s preparatory role.
verses.before: As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way;
verses.after: As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way.”
verses.tsw_comparator: As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way;

verses.rationale: Lineates the wilderness summons while keeping the road image.
verses.before: a voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.’”
verses.after: “A voice cries out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the Lord’s way; make his paths straight.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: a voice crying in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves baptism, repentance, and forgiveness without making one relationship more explicit than the Greek.
verses.before: John appeared in the wilderness, baptizing and proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
verses.after: John the baptizer appeared in the wilderness, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: John appeared, baptizing in the wilderness and proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sweeping geographical description and confession linked to baptism.
verses.before: People from all across Judea and all the people of Jerusalem were going out to him. They were baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
verses.after: People from all Judea and all Jerusalem went out to him. Confessing their sins, they were baptized by him in the Jordan River.
verses.tsw_comparator: And all the region of Judea and all the people of Jerusalem were going out to him, and they were baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.

verses.rationale: Preserves material, belt, and actual foods without symbolic substitution.
verses.before: John wore clothing made of camel’s hair with a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.
verses.after: John wore camel-hair clothing with a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now John was clothed with camel’s hair and wore a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.

verses.rationale: Retains comparative strength and the lowly sandal action.
verses.before: He proclaimed, “After me comes one stronger than I am. I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the strap of his sandals.
verses.after: He proclaimed, “Someone stronger than I am is coming after me. I am not worthy to stoop down and untie his sandal straps.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he proclaimed, saying, “After me comes one stronger than I, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.

verses.rationale: Preserves water/Spirit contrast without importing fire from other Gospels.
verses.before: I baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
verses.after: I have baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”

verses.rationale: Retains origin, baptizer, and river.
verses.before: In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
verses.after: In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
verses.tsw_comparator: In those days Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.

verses.rationale: Preserves immediate perception, torn heavens, and simile rather than identifying the Spirit as a bird.
verses.before: As soon as he came up out of the water, he saw the heavens being torn open and the Spirit descending on him like a dove.
verses.after: As he came up out of the water, he immediately saw the heavens being torn open and the Spirit descending on him like a dove.
verses.tsw_comparator: And immediately, as he came up out of the water, he saw the heavens being torn open and the Spirit descending on him like a dove.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct second-person address and divine delight.
verses.before: And a voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son; with you I am well pleased.”
verses.after: A voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son; I am well pleased with you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And a voice came from the heavens: “You are my beloved Son; with you I am well pleased.”

verses.rationale: Retains Mark’s forceful drove and urgency.
verses.before: Immediately the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness.
verses.after: At once the Spirit drove him into the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: And immediately the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Preserves duration, adversary, animals, and angelic service without adding three temptations.
verses.before: He was in the wilderness forty days, being tested by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and the angels were serving him.
verses.after: He was in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and the angels served him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he was in the wilderness forty days, being tested by Satan. And he was with the wild animals, and the angels were serving him.

verses.rationale: Keeps handed-over language and the pinned God’s-good-news form.
verses.before: After John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee proclaiming the good news of God.
verses.after: After John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee proclaiming God’s good news.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the good news of God,

verses.rationale: Preserves fulfilled time, nearness, and the two imperatives.
verses.before: He said, “The time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near. Repent and trust the good news.”
verses.after: “The time is fulfilled,” he said. “The kingdom of God has drawn near. Repent and believe the good news.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and saying, “The time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near. Repent, and trust in the good news.”

verses.rationale: Names the brothers clearly and retains their work as the setting.
verses.before: As Jesus passed along the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Simon’s brother Andrew casting a net into the sea, because they were fishermen.
verses.after: As he walked beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Simon’s brother Andrew casting a net into the sea; they were fishermen.
verses.tsw_comparator: Passing along the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting a net into the sea, for they were fishers.

verses.rationale: Preserves the occupational metaphor with an inclusive human referent.
verses.before: Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you become fishers of people.”
verses.after: Jesus said to them, “Come, follow me, and I will make you fishers of people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you become fishers of people.”

verses.rationale: Retains the immediate response and abandoned equipment.
verses.before: Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
verses.after: At once they left their nets and followed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And immediately they left their nets and followed him.

verses.rationale: Renders net preparation without insisting on repair alone.
verses.before: Going a little farther, he saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John in their boat, mending the nets.
verses.after: A little farther on, he saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John in their boat, putting their nets in order.
verses.tsw_comparator: And going on a little farther, he saw James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, who were in their boat mending the nets.

verses.rationale: Retains urgency and the hired workers who remain with the father.
verses.before: Immediately he called them. They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers and went after him.
verses.after: He called them at once. They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers and went after him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And immediately he called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired servants and went after him.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned shorter reading without adding an entry verb absent here.
verses.before: They went into Capernaum, and on the Sabbath Jesus entered the synagogue and began to teach.
verses.after: They went into Capernaum. On the Sabbath he immediately began teaching in the synagogue.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they went into Capernaum. And immediately on the Sabbath he entered the synagogue and was teaching.

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit comparison without defining the scribes’ motives.
verses.before: The people were astonished at his teaching, because he taught them as one who had authority, and not as the scribes.
verses.after: The people were astonished at his teaching, for he taught them with authority, unlike the scribes.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they were astonished at his teaching, for he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sudden interruption and the spirit’s description.
verses.before: Just then, a man in their synagogue who had an unclean spirit cried out,
verses.after: Just then a man with an unclean spirit was in their synagogue. He cried out,
verses.tsw_comparator: And immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit; and he cried out,

verses.rationale: Preserves plural us, singular I, and the identifying title.
verses.before: “What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God!”
verses.after: “What have you to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God!”
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, “What have you to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God!”

verses.rationale: Keeps both commands and distinguishes the spirit from the man.
verses.before: Jesus rebuked the spirit: “Be silent and come out of him!”
verses.after: Jesus rebuked the spirit: “Be silent and come out of him!”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent, and come out of him.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the physical convulsion and audible departure.
verses.before: The unclean spirit convulsed the man, cried out with a loud voice, and came out of him.
verses.after: The unclean spirit convulsed the man and came out of him with a loud cry.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the unclean spirit, convulsing him and crying out with a loud voice, came out of him.

verses.rationale: Connects authority to the crowd’s astonished interpretation.
verses.before: Everyone was amazed, and they began asking one another, “What is this? A new teaching—with authority! He even commands the unclean spirits, and they obey him.”
verses.after: Everyone was amazed. They asked one another, “What is this? A new teaching with authority! He even commands unclean spirits, and they obey him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And they were all amazed, so that they questioned among themselves, saying, “What is this? A new teaching—with authority! He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him.”

verses.rationale: Retains urgency and the geographical spread without enlarging it beyond the region.
verses.before: News about him spread at once throughout the surrounding region of Galilee.
verses.after: News of him immediately spread everywhere throughout the surrounding region of Galilee.
verses.tsw_comparator: And at once his fame went out everywhere, throughout the whole surrounding region of Galilee.

verses.rationale: Retains the plural departure in the pinned source and all named companions.
verses.before: As soon as they left the synagogue, they went with James and John to the home of Simon and Andrew.
verses.after: As soon as they left the synagogue, they went to Simon and Andrew’s house with James and John.
verses.tsw_comparator: And immediately, when they came out of the synagogue, they went into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the illness and recipient of the report.
verses.before: Simon’s mother-in-law was in bed with a fever, and they immediately told Jesus about her.
verses.after: Simon’s mother-in-law was lying down with a fever. They told Jesus about her at once.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Simon’s mother-in-law was lying sick with a fever, and immediately they told him about her.

verses.rationale: Preserves touch, raising, healing, and her own subsequent action.
verses.before: He went to her, took her by the hand, and raised her up. The fever left her, and she began to serve them.
verses.after: He went to her, took her hand, and raised her up. The fever left her, and she began serving them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he came and took her by the hand and raised her up; and the fever left her, and she began to serve them.

verses.rationale: Retains both evening markers and distinguishes illness from demon affliction.
verses.before: That evening, after the sun had set, people brought to him everyone who was sick or oppressed by demons.
verses.after: That evening, after sunset, they brought him everyone who was ill or afflicted by demons.
verses.tsw_comparator: That evening, when the sun had set, they brought to him all who were sick or oppressed by demons.

verses.rationale: Preserves the narrator’s sweeping crowd description without a numerical gloss.
verses.before: The whole city gathered at the door.
verses.after: The whole town gathered at the door.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the whole city was gathered together at the door.

verses.rationale: Retains many, varied illnesses, and the stated reason for silence.
verses.before: He healed many who were sick with various diseases and cast out many demons. He would not allow the demons to speak, because they knew him.
verses.after: He healed many with various diseases and drove out many demons. He would not let the demons speak, because they knew him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he healed many who were sick with various diseases, and he cast out many demons. And he would not permit the demons to speak, because they knew him.

verses.rationale: Preserves darkness, withdrawal, and prayer in clear sequence.
verses.before: Very early in the morning, while it was still dark, Jesus got up, went out to a deserted place, and prayed there.
verses.after: Very early, while it was still dark, he got up and went out to a deserted place. There he prayed.
verses.tsw_comparator: And rising very early in the morning, while it was still dark, he went out and departed to a desolate place, and there he prayed.

verses.rationale: Keeps the active pursuit without adding hostility.
verses.before: Simon and those with him went looking for him.
verses.after: Simon and his companions went looking for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Simon and those with him searched for him,

verses.rationale: Retains the disciples’ sweeping report as their speech.
verses.before: When they found him, they said, “Everyone is looking for you.”
verses.after: When they found him, they said, “Everyone is looking for you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and they found him and said to him, “Everyone is looking for you.”

verses.rationale: Retains the purpose and ambiguous came-out expression rather than specifying a heavenly origin.
verses.before: He said to them, “Let us go somewhere else, to the nearby towns, so that I may proclaim there too. This is why I came out.”
verses.after: He answered, “Let us go elsewhere, to the nearby towns, so I can proclaim the message there too. That is why I came out.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Let us go on to the neighboring towns, so that I may proclaim there also, for this is why I came out.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the paired activities and regional scope.
verses.before: So he went throughout Galilee, proclaiming in their synagogues and casting out demons.
verses.after: He went throughout Galilee, proclaiming the message in their synagogues and driving out demons.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he went throughout all Galilee, proclaiming in their synagogues and casting out demons.

verses.rationale: Keeps the appeal about willingness, not ability, and clean language.
verses.before: A man with a skin disease came to him, pleading with him and kneeling. He said, “If you are willing, you can make me clean.”
verses.after: A man with leprosy came to him, knelt, and pleaded, “If you are willing, you can make me clean.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And a man with leprosy came to him, pleading with him and kneeling, and saying to him, “If you are willing, you can make me clean.”

verses.rationale: Follows pinned anger without substituting the compassion variant or inventing an object for the anger.
verses.before: Moved with anger, Jesus reached out his hand, touched him, and said, “I am willing. Be made clean.”
verses.after: Moved to anger, Jesus reached out his hand and touched him. “I am willing,” he said. “Be clean.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand and touched him and said to him, “I am willing. Be made clean.”

verses.rationale: Preserves immediate cleansing and the passive description.
verses.before: Immediately the disease left him, and he was made clean.
verses.after: At once the leprosy left him, and he was made clean.
verses.tsw_comparator: And immediately the leprosy left him, and he was made clean.

verses.rationale: Carries the force of the warning and dismissal without adding an emotional explanation.
verses.before: Jesus sternly warned him and sent him away at once.
verses.after: Jesus sternly warned him and immediately sent him away.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he sternly warned him and immediately sent him away,

verses.rationale: Retains silence, priestly presentation, offering, and the open-ended testimony phrase.
verses.before: He said, “See that you say nothing to anyone. Go, show yourself to the priest and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
verses.after: “See that you tell no one anything,” he said. “Instead, go, show yourself to the priest, and offer what Moses commanded for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and said to him, “See that you say nothing to anyone, but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”

verses.rationale: Makes the cause and effect clear and distinguishes Jesus from the healed man.
verses.before: But the man went out and began proclaiming the matter freely and spreading the news. As a result, Jesus could no longer enter a town openly but stayed outside in deserted places. Yet people kept coming to him from everywhere.
verses.after: But the man went out and began telling the news widely. As a result, Jesus could no longer enter a town openly. He stayed outside in deserted places, but people kept coming to him from everywhere.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he went out and began to proclaim it freely and to spread the matter around, so that Jesus could no longer openly enter a town, but was outside in desolate places; and people were coming to him from everywhere.

verses.rationale: Renders the time interval and home idiom while recording the house alternative in a note.
verses.before: When Jesus returned to Capernaum after some days, word spread that he was at home.
verses.after: A few days later, Jesus returned to Capernaum, and word spread that he was at home.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when he returned to Capernaum after some days, it was heard that he was at home.

verses.rationale: Preserves overcrowding and the continuing teaching.
verses.before: So many people gathered that there was no more room, not even near the door, and he was speaking the word to them.
verses.after: So many gathered that there was no room left, not even at the door. He was speaking the message to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And many were gathered, so that there was no longer room, not even at the door; and he was speaking the word to them.

verses.rationale: Retains four carriers without inventing friendship or their names.
verses.before: Some people came bringing a paralyzed man, carried by four of them.
verses.after: Some people came bringing a paralyzed man, carried by four of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they came, bringing to him a paralytic carried by four.

verses.rationale: Preserves both roof opening and digging without imposing a modern roof structure.
verses.before: Since they could not get him to Jesus because of the crowd, they opened the roof above him. After digging through it, they lowered the mat on which the man was lying.
verses.after: Unable to bring him to Jesus because of the crowd, they opened the roof above him. They dug through it and lowered the mat on which the paralyzed man lay.
verses.tsw_comparator: And not being able to bring him to Jesus because of the crowd, they removed the roof above him, and when they had broken it open, they lowered the mat on which the paralytic lay.

verses.rationale: Retains their faith and the passive forgiveness declaration.
verses.before: When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralyzed man, “Child, your sins are forgiven.”
verses.after: Seeing their faith, Jesus said to the paralyzed man, “Child, your sins are forgiven.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Child, your sins are forgiven.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the internal rather than spoken objection.
verses.before: Some scribes were sitting there, reasoning in their hearts,
verses.after: Some scribes were sitting there, reasoning within themselves,
verses.tsw_comparator: Now some of the scribes were sitting there, reasoning in their hearts,

verses.rationale: Keeps blasphemy as their charge and the question about authority.
verses.before: “Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming. Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
verses.after: “Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Why does this one speak in this way? He is blaspheming. Who can forgive sins except God alone?”

verses.rationale: Preserves spirit and hearts rather than adding a theory of perception.
verses.before: Immediately Jesus knew in his spirit that they were reasoning this way within themselves. He said to them, “Why are you reasoning these things in your hearts?
verses.after: Jesus immediately recognized in his spirit what they were thinking. He asked them, “Why are you reasoning like this in your hearts?
verses.tsw_comparator: And immediately Jesus, perceiving in his spirit that they were reasoning within themselves, said to them, “Why do you reason these things in your hearts?

verses.rationale: Keeps the contrast between two spoken commands rather than reframing which deed is easier.
verses.before: Which is easier: to say to the paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?
verses.after: Which is easier: to tell the paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, take your mat, and walk’?
verses.tsw_comparator: Which is easier, to say to the paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Rise, take up your mat and walk’?

verses.rationale: Preserves the interrupted speech and the narrator’s change of addressee.
verses.before: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralyzed man—
verses.after: But so that you may know the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralyzed man,
verses.tsw_comparator: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralytic—

verses.rationale: Retains the three commands and direct address.
verses.before: “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
verses.after: “I tell you, get up, take your mat, and go home.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “I say to you, rise, take up your mat, and go to your house.”

verses.rationale: Preserves immediate visible response and communal praise.
verses.before: He got up, immediately picked up the mat, and walked out in front of everyone. They were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this.”
verses.after: He got up, immediately picked up his mat, and walked out in front of everyone. They were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he rose and immediately took up the mat and went out before them all, so that all were amazed and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the return to the shore and ongoing teaching.
verses.before: Jesus went out again beside the sea. The whole crowd came to him, and he taught them.
verses.after: Jesus went out beside the sea again. The whole crowd came to him, and he taught them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he went out again beside the sea, and all the crowd was coming to him, and he was teaching them.

verses.rationale: Names the responder without identifying him as Matthew from another Gospel.
verses.before: As he passed by, he saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth. Jesus said to him, “Follow me.” Levi got up and followed him.
verses.after: As he passed by, he saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth. “Follow me,” he said. Levi got up and followed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him, “Follow me.” And he rose and followed him.

verses.rationale: Chooses Levi as the house’s owner with the pronoun ambiguity recorded in a note.
verses.before: Later, as Jesus was reclining at the table in Levi’s house, many tax collectors and sinners were eating with Jesus and his disciples, because many of them were following him.
verses.after: As Jesus reclined at the table in Levi’s house, many tax collectors and sinners ate with him and his disciples, for many were following him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened that he was reclining at table in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Jesus and his disciples, for many were following him.

verses.rationale: Follows scribes of the Pharisees rather than treating them as two separate groups.
verses.before: When the scribes of the Pharisees saw him eating with sinners and tax collectors, they asked his disciples, “Why does he eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
verses.after: When the scribes of the Pharisees saw him eating with sinners and tax collectors, they asked his disciples, “Why does he eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the scribes of the Pharisees, seeing that he was eating with sinners and tax collectors, said to his disciples, “Why does he eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the doctor analogy and omits to-repentance absent from this source.
verses.before: Jesus heard them and said, “Those who are healthy do not need a physician, but those who are sick do. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”
verses.after: Jesus heard this and said, “Healthy people do not need a doctor; sick people do. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And hearing, Jesus said to them, “Those who are strong have no need of a physician, but those who are ill. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the questioners unspecified and preserves the contrasted groups.
verses.before: John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. People came and asked Jesus, “Why do John’s disciples and the Pharisees’ disciples fast, but your disciples do not?”
verses.after: John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. People came and asked Jesus, “Why do John’s disciples and the Pharisees’ disciples fast, but yours do not?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the disciples of John and the Pharisees were fasting, and they came and said to him, “Why do the disciples of John and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?”

verses.rationale: Renders sons-of-the-wedding-chamber idiom naturally and retains the repetition.
verses.before: Jesus said to them, “Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
verses.after: Jesus answered, “Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus said to them, “Can the sons of the wedding chamber fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.

verses.rationale: Preserves taken-away passive and the shift from days to that day.
verses.before: But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them. Then, on that day, they will fast.
verses.after: But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them. Then, on that day, they will fast.
verses.tsw_comparator: The days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast in that day.

verses.rationale: Makes the contrasting materials and resulting damage clear without replacing the image with an application.
verses.before: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment. Otherwise the new patch pulls away from the old cloth, and the tear becomes worse.
verses.after: “No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment. Otherwise the new patch pulls away from the old cloth, and the tear becomes worse.
verses.tsw_comparator: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; otherwise the patch pulls away from it, the new from the old, and a worse tear is made.

verses.rationale: Preserves both losses and supplies belongs for the final elliptical instruction.
verses.before: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise the wine will burst the skins, and both the wine and the skins will be lost. New wine goes into fresh wineskins.”
verses.after: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise the wine bursts the skins, and both the wine and the skins are ruined. New wine belongs in fresh wineskins.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wine will burst the skins, and the wine is lost, and so are the skins; but new wine is for fresh wineskins.”

verses.rationale: Preserves walking and plucking without adding an explicit eating verb absent here.
verses.before: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields, and his disciples began making their way while plucking heads of grain.
verses.after: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through grainfields. As his disciples made their way along, they began plucking heads of grain.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened that he was passing through grainfields on the Sabbath, and his disciples began to make a path, plucking heads of grain.

verses.rationale: Keeps the legal accusation in the speakers’ question.
verses.before: The Pharisees said to him, “Look! Why are they doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?”
verses.after: The Pharisees said to him, “Look! Why are they doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the Pharisees were saying to him, “Look, why are they doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?”

verses.rationale: Retains the appeal to reading and the shared need.
verses.before: He said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he and those with him were in need and hungry?
verses.after: He answered, “Have you never read what David did when he and his companions were hungry and in need?
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he had need and was hungry, he and those with him,

verses.rationale: Preserves Abiathar rather than silently reconciling the name with Samuel.
verses.before: He entered the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the bread of the Presence, which no one except the priests is permitted to eat, and he also gave some to those who were with him.”
verses.after: He entered God’s house in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the bread of the Presence, which only priests may lawfully eat. He also gave some to those with him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: how he entered the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the bread of the Presence, which it is not lawful for any to eat except the priests, and also gave it to those with him?”

verses.rationale: Renders the generic human referent inclusively and retains the reversal.
verses.before: Then Jesus said to them, “The Sabbath was made for humanity, not humanity for the Sabbath.
verses.after: Then he told them, “The Sabbath was made for humanity, not humanity for the Sabbath.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “The Sabbath came to be for the sake of humanity, and not humanity for the Sabbath.

verses.rationale: Preserves the title and even-Sabbath conclusion.
verses.before: So the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”
verses.after: So the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the return and specific bodily condition.
verses.before: Jesus entered the synagogue again, and a man with a withered hand was there.
verses.after: Jesus entered a synagogue again. A man with a withered hand was there.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he entered again into a synagogue, and there was a man there who had a withered hand.

verses.rationale: Keeps the watchers unnamed here and makes their stated purpose clear.
verses.before: They were watching Jesus closely to see whether he would heal the man on the Sabbath, so that they could accuse him.
verses.after: They watched Jesus closely to see whether he would heal the man on the Sabbath, so they could accuse him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they were watching him closely, whether he would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they might accuse him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the public placement before the challenge.
verses.before: Jesus said to the man with the withered hand, “Stand up here in front of everyone.”
verses.after: He told the man with the withered hand, “Stand up here in the middle.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to the man who had the withered hand, “Rise into the midst.”

verses.rationale: Retains both ethical contrasts and the silence.
verses.before: Then he asked them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save a life or to kill?” But they were silent.
verses.after: Then he asked them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save a life or to kill?” But they remained silent.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save life or to kill?” But they were silent.

verses.rationale: Preserves anger and grief together, followed by command and restoration.
verses.before: Looking around at them with anger and deeply grieved at the hardness of their hearts, Jesus said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
verses.after: He looked around at them in anger, grieved by their hardened hearts. He told the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
verses.tsw_comparator: And looking around at them with anger, grieved at the hardness of their heart, he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored.

verses.rationale: Retains urgency, alliance, and lethal intent.
verses.before: The Pharisees went out and immediately began plotting with the Herodians against Jesus, discussing how they might destroy him.
verses.after: The Pharisees went out and immediately began plotting with the Herodians how to destroy him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the Pharisees went out and immediately held counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the first geographical group and allows the list to cross the verse boundary.
verses.before: Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea, and a great crowd followed from Galilee and Judea,
verses.after: Jesus withdrew to the sea with his disciples, and a large crowd from Galilee followed. People also came from Judea,
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea, and a great multitude from Galilee followed, and from Judea,

verses.rationale: Preserves all listed regions and the reason for coming.
verses.before: from Jerusalem, Idumea, beyond the Jordan, and the regions around Tyre and Sidon. A great crowd came to him because they had heard what he was doing.
verses.after: Jerusalem, Idumea, beyond the Jordan, and the area around Tyre and Sidon. Hearing all he was doing, a great crowd came to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: and from Jerusalem and Idumea and beyond the Jordan and around Tyre and Sidon—a great multitude, hearing what he was doing, came to him.

verses.rationale: Makes the boat’s protective purpose explicit from the source.
verses.before: Because of the crowd, he told his disciples to have a small boat ready for him so that the people would not crush him.
verses.after: Because of the crowd, he told his disciples to keep a small boat ready for him so that people would not crush him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he told his disciples to have a small boat ready for him because of the crowd, lest they crush him,

verses.rationale: Preserves the crowd’s physical pressure and motive.
verses.before: He had healed many, so everyone who had an affliction pressed toward him to touch him.
verses.after: He had healed many, so everyone with an affliction pressed toward him to touch him.
verses.tsw_comparator: for he had healed many, so that all who had afflictions pressed upon him in order to touch him.

verses.rationale: Preserves recurring recognition and the explicit title.
verses.before: Whenever the unclean spirits saw him, they fell down before him and cried out, “You are the Son of God!”
verses.after: Whenever the unclean spirits saw him, they fell before him and cried out, “You are the Son of God!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And whenever the unclean spirits saw him, they fell down before him and cried out, saying, “You are the Son of God.”

verses.rationale: Retains the strong prohibition without explaining its motive.
verses.before: But he repeatedly ordered them not to make him known.
verses.after: He sternly ordered them not to make him known.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he strictly ordered them not to make him known.

verses.rationale: Preserves Jesus’ selection and their response without naming an unstated mountain.
verses.before: Jesus went up on the mountain and called those he wanted, and they came to him.
verses.after: He went up the mountain and called those he wanted, and they came to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he went up on the mountain and called to him those whom he wanted, and they came to him.

verses.rationale: Retains being-with and being-sent; omits the apostles clause absent from the pinned text.
verses.before: He appointed twelve, whom he also named apostles, so that they might be with him and so that he might send them out to proclaim,
verses.after: He appointed twelve to be with him and to be sent out to proclaim the message,
verses.tsw_comparator: And he appointed twelve, whom he also named apostles, so that they might be with him and that he might send them out to proclaim,

verses.rationale: Preserves the stated authority without adding a healing commission absent here.
verses.before: and to have authority to cast out demons.
verses.after: with authority to drive out demons.
verses.tsw_comparator: and to have authority to cast out demons.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated appointment and Simon’s new name.
verses.before: He appointed the twelve: Simon, to whom he gave the name Peter;
verses.after: These are the twelve he appointed: Simon, whom he named Peter;
verses.tsw_comparator: And he appointed the twelve: Simon (to whom he gave the name Peter),

verses.rationale: Retains the brothers’ relationship and the unexplained nickname’s translation.
verses.before: James son of Zebedee and John the brother of James, to whom he gave the name Boanerges, that is, Sons of Thunder;
verses.after: James son of Zebedee and John, James’s brother, whom he named Boanerges, meaning “Sons of Thunder”;
verses.tsw_comparator: and James the son of Zebedee and John the brother of James (to whom he gave the name Boanerges, that is, Sons of Thunder),

verses.rationale: Preserves the complete list and the source designation rather than changing it to Canaanite.
verses.before: Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot,
verses.after: Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Cananaean,
verses.tsw_comparator: and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Zealot,

verses.rationale: Preserves the final name and the hand-over motif.
verses.before: and Judas Iscariot, who later handed him over.
verses.after: and Judas Iscariot, who handed him over.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

verses.rationale: Makes the plural group clear and preserves the inability to eat.
verses.before: Then Jesus went into a house, and the crowd gathered again, so that they could not even eat.
verses.after: Then he went home. Again a crowd gathered, so that he and his disciples could not even eat.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he came into a house, and the crowd gathered again, so that they were not even able to eat bread.

verses.rationale: Chooses family for those-with-him with the broader associates reading noted; preserves their alarming claim.
verses.before: When those close to him heard about it, they went out to restrain him, because they were saying, “He is out of his mind.”
verses.after: When his family heard, they went out to take charge of him, for they were saying, “He is out of his mind.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And hearing it, those beside him went out to seize him, for they were saying, “He is out of his mind.”

verses.rationale: Keeps two accusations in the scribes’ speech.
verses.before: The scribes who came down from Jerusalem were saying, “He has Beelzebul,” and, “He casts out demons by the ruler of the demons.”
verses.after: The scribes who had come down from Jerusalem said, “He has Beelzebul,” and, “He drives out demons by the ruler of demons.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the scribes who came down from Jerusalem were saying, “He has Beelzebul,” and “By the ruler of the demons he casts out demons.”

verses.rationale: Retains the summons and self-defeating accusation as a question.
verses.before: Jesus called them to himself and spoke to them in parables: “How can Satan cast out Satan?
verses.after: Jesus called them over and spoke to them in parables: “How can Satan drive out Satan?
verses.tsw_comparator: And calling them to him, he spoke to them in parables, “How can Satan cast out Satan?

verses.rationale: Preserves the kingdom image and repeated referent.
verses.before: If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
verses.after: If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom is not able to stand.

verses.rationale: Keeps the parallel household image without reducing it to a building.
verses.before: If a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.
verses.after: If a household is divided against itself, that household cannot stand.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.

verses.rationale: Makes the inference clear while retaining self-division and ending.
verses.before: And if Satan has risen up against himself and is divided, he cannot stand; his end has come.
verses.after: And if Satan has risen against himself and is divided, he cannot stand; his end has come.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if Satan has risen up against himself and is divided, he is not able to stand, but has come to an end.

verses.rationale: Preserves the necessary prior restraint and subsequent plundering.
verses.before: But no one can enter a strong man’s house and plunder his possessions unless he first binds the strong man. Then he can plunder the house.
verses.after: But no one can enter a strong man’s house and plunder his possessions without first tying up the strong man. Only then can his house be plundered.
verses.tsw_comparator: But no one can enter the house of the strong man and plunder his goods unless he first binds the strong man, and then he will plunder his house.

verses.rationale: Renders sons-of-humans generically and retains the wide scope of forgiveness.
verses.before: Truly I tell you, all sins will be forgiven the children of humanity, and whatever blasphemies they speak;
verses.after: I tell you the truth: people will be forgiven all their sins and whatever blasphemies they utter.
verses.tsw_comparator: Truly I say to you, all sins will be forgiven the children of humanity, and whatever blasphemies they may utter;

verses.rationale: Preserves eternal sin rather than substituting the judgment variant.
verses.before: but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness and is guilty of an eternal sin.”
verses.after: But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never have forgiveness and is guilty of an eternal sin.”
verses.tsw_comparator: but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is guilty of an eternal sin—

verses.rationale: Makes the narrator’s explanatory link and repeated accusation explicit.
verses.before: He said this because they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.”
verses.after: He said this because they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.”
verses.tsw_comparator: for they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the outside location and indirect summons.
verses.before: His mother and brothers came, and standing outside they sent word to him and called for him.
verses.after: His mother and his brothers arrived. Standing outside, they sent word to him and called for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And his mother and his brothers came, and standing outside they sent to him, calling him.

verses.rationale: Retains the reported family members without adding sisters absent here.
verses.before: A crowd was sitting around him, and they said, “Look, your mother and your brothers are outside looking for you.”
verses.after: A crowd was sitting around him. They told him, “Your mother and your brothers are outside looking for you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And a crowd was sitting around him, and they said to him, “Behold, your mother and your brothers are outside, seeking you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the question leading into a redefinition of kinship.
verses.before: He answered them, “Who are my mother and my brothers?”
verses.after: He answered, “Who are my mother and my brothers?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And answering them he said, “Who are my mother and my brothers?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the gesture toward actual listeners and the announced relationship.
verses.before: Looking around at those sitting in a circle around him, he said, “Here are my mother and my brothers!
verses.after: Looking around at those seated in a circle around him, he said, “Here are my mother and my brothers!
verses.tsw_comparator: And looking around at those sitting in a circle around him, he said, “Behold my mother and my brothers!

verses.rationale: Preserves all three kinship terms including explicit sister.
verses.before: Whoever does the will of God is my brother and sister and mother.”
verses.after: Whoever does God’s will is my brother and sister and mother.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever does the will of God, this one is my brother and sister and mother.”
